title: Opening with Armstrong at the Zanzibar
summary: He opened the same night he was fitted, on a bill with Bill Robinson and other acts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I called Glaser and Joe Glaser said to Go to Karnak, tailor shop at 48th and 7th Avenue so I was fitted with three uniforms, one was dark blue with white buttons and another one was light blue, sky-blue and the third one was gray, gray pants and gray sport coat. That morning I reported for my measurements and late afternoon those uniforms were ready to be worn. That night I opened with Louie at the Zanzibar on 49th and Broadway. And on the same bill at the Zanzibar was Bill Robinson, the Delta Rhythm Boys, the Peters Sisters, Maurice Rocco, Pee Wee Marquette. The intermission band was Claude Hopkins and our band and then we'd get off played the show, some dancing, and then we'd get Claude Hopkins to take over.
Did Claude Hopkins have a small group at that time or was it an orchestra?
He only had about seven men. We had the big band. It was beautiful to hear Louie play. I'd be listening while reading my music and we had a head arrangement. I'd listen to Louis.
This was in 1944, around what time of the year? The latter part of the year?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
So this was at the Zanzibar. And how long did that engagement last?
Perhaps about two months, roughly two months, a few weeks.
